scope: Single-block decryption; all candidates use existing round keys and inverse LUT objects. No Cipher layout/API change or new key-dependent table.

method.input: Runtime random startup key and arbitrary ciphertext; subsequent calls consume previous output.
method.discovery: 7 or 9 repeated samples, 0.5 or 1 million calls per sample; untimed warmup.
method.paired: 31 alternating candidate/baseline pairs, 500000 calls per sample; both outputs compared exactly.
method.api_shape: Candidate wrapper receives Cipher by value before calling keys-only kernel, matching public Cipher.decrypt.
method.baseline: Exact src/scalar.zig raw-first fused inverse lookup and scalar final S-inverse.
method.contention: No known concurrent experiment on assigned CPU core; short frequency/host variation remains, so decisions use alternating paired ratios rather than cross-run absolute differences.

selected.group_assignment: Remaining positions distributed by (position-5)%3. Seed next inverse key into first partial chain. Force GPR partial reduction before merging inverse-affine GFNI sum.
selected.first_round: Raw ciphertext maps to AES field for compressed contributions; remaining LUT indices use Pi(ciphertext byte), canceling the inverse S inside each LUT.
selected.final_round: Two 512-bit VPERMI2B lookups plus a byte-mask blend implement final inverse S, using only low 16 result bytes.
selected.features: LLVM plus native GFNI / AVX-512 VBMI and AVX512VL; production dispatch is CPU/feature gated separately.
selected.note: Four GPR chains also won strongly and were effectively tied; three were selected to share the encryption configuration. Final compact production layout must be remeasured because register allocation/code placement can shift the small differences.

correctness.normal_contributions: All16 input rows ×256 byte values matched existing inverse LUT contributions.
correctness.raw_first_contributions: All16 input rows ×256 values matched inverse LUT[row][Pi[value]].
correctness.independent_reference: Four keys ×16 arbitrary ciphertexts compared against basic L-inverse, S-inverse and key transformations; then16 keys ×64 arbitrary ciphertexts compared against current exact scalar. Every candidate and compact variant checked.
correctness.endpoint: Every256 inverse S-box values checked against the table.
correctness.suites: All21 tests passed for original hybrid, endpoints, AES-resident, GPR, dense-chain and first-round-count variants. Timed workload checksums also agreed.

decisions.hypothesis: Partial inverse LUT rows computed by GFNI but remaining state accumulated as vectors
decisions.result: Only modest improvement after raw-first and VBMI endpoint; inferior to GPR scheduling.

decisions.hypothesis: Keep entire inter-round state and normal lookup reduction in GPRs; compute only compressed partial in SIMD
decisions.result: Accepted: about21% lower API-shaped latency versus current exact scalar.

decisions.hypothesis: Move all intermediate state to AES field to remove inverse-affine from the message dependency
decisions.result: Rejected:52.98–63.72ns versus roughly53ns control; extra mapped indices/key transforms outweigh saved affine.

decisions.hypothesis: Final VBMI endpoint alone on current scalar
decisions.result: About3–4% gain; does not explain the larger compressed hybrid gain.
Rejected: leading5 worsened roughly6%; leading6 effectively flat. Memory-folded coefficients retained.
Two/three/four close; one slower. Three adopted as common encryption/decryption configuration.
Compression8 instead of5 saved less than1% in discovery, rejected extra policy. Compression0 regressed by~5ns and reactivated discarded LUT rows.

perf.scope: Whole isolated process, fixed PRNG seed; same checksum; startup negligible relative to20M chained decryptions.
perf.events_note: cycles and instructions are useful here. Generic L1-dcache-load-misses are suspiciously low for this workload under this VM and are preserved as raw observations, not used to prove a cache-miss mechanism.

limitations: Results apply to measured native Zen5 single-block hot repeated calls; other CPUs retain separately measured paths.
This finite hypothesis study cannot prove a physical global optimum.
No new constant-time/security property is claimed; the original implementation and these candidates use secret-dependent table indices.
